activity_title: Discover the authoritative pack source before writing any classification code
activity_summary: Phase 1 was discovery only, with no code edited. Found inventory.product_pk, 28 rows mapping pack_char to pack_qty (A=10 through S=25 and 1 to 9), and made the build read it on every run so no pack code is ever hardcoded in Python or JavaScript. Confirmed the rule holds database-wide: 7,190 pack SKUs with zero false positives, while 5,901 SKUs containing a plus sign merely carry pack tokens and must stay COMBO.
evidence_refs: 28 pack codes read from inventory.product_pk; 7,190 pack SKUs, 0 false positives; 5,901 plus-SKUs unaffected
reusable_pattern: Find the database's own reference table for a classification before inventing a regex
validation_rule: Pack codes are read from the source table every build, never hardcoded

activity_title: Implement Component, Combo and Pack as a single source of truth
activity_summary: Classification happens only in build_v2.py and travels in the payload as B["cls"]; the UI filters on that value and holds no regex of its own. A SKU containing a plus sign is never a Pack. Precedence is authoritative pack table, then PACK, then an existing combo relationship, then COMBO, then COMPONENT. The build also reports component_products_classified_pack so a future in-scope pack SKU is classified automatically rather than silently missed.
evidence_refs: main 311 components / 257 combos / 156 packs; all data 677 / 407 / 211; component_products_classified_pack = 0
reusable_pattern: Classify once in the builder and ship the label in the payload so no two layers can disagree
validation_rule: No classification regex may exist in the JavaScript layer

activity_title: Add the Packs tab and restate the counts as distinct products
activity_summary: Packs became a third first-class view alongside Components and Combos, and the phone breakpoint was compacted so three tabs still fit at 375px. The count line was redefined to report distinct products rather than marketplace rows: Combo Components 128 and Pack Count 211 on the All Data scope. This closed the long-running confusion where a badge of 802 was read as a product count when it was really marketplace rows for 411 products.
evidence_refs: Combo Components 128; Pack Count 211; 677 + 407 + 211 = 1,295 products; 375px layout has no overflow
reusable_pattern: State the unit on every count so a row total is never mistaken for a product total
validation_rule: Counts on screen are distinct products unless the label says rows

activity_title: Prove the classification change altered nothing else
activity_summary: The pre-change builder was re-run against the same database and compared field by field with the new one. Every value was identical and the only difference was the added cls field. Reconciliation closed on every population: 677 plus 407 plus 211 equals 1,295; 795 relationships equal 584 combo plus 211 pack; zero missing, zero extra, zero duplicate and zero multi-category products.
evidence_refs: all fields identical before vs after; only cls added; 0 missing / 0 extra / 0 duplicate / 0 multi-category
reusable_pattern: Re-run the previous build against the same data to prove a refactor is non-functional
validation_rule: A classification change must leave every existing field byte-identical

activity_title: Make the 11:00 refresh survive a temporary connection-limit refusal
activity_summary: The cron had failed on 15 and 16 September with FATAL too many connections for role tech_user, aborting on a single connection attempt. Stage 1 now retries up to three times with waits of 30 then 60 seconds, and only on a connection-capacity refusal. Every other failure class, meaning Python errors, SQL errors and hard validation failures, still fails on the first attempt, and publish is skipped whenever no fresh build exists so stale output can never be pushed.
evidence_refs: harness: transient refusal retried 3 times with waits; hard failure not retried; failed build skipped compose and publish
reusable_pattern: Retry only the one condition you can name, and prove the negative case is still not retried
validation_rule: A failed fresh build must never lead to a publish
gap_or_risk: The retry is a mitigation; the database still saturates its connection limit at 11:00
next_action: Ask the database team about the 11:00 connection saturation

activity_title: Publish the validated build to the AIOS hub under control and read it back
activity_summary: Files were staged explicitly rather than with git add dot, then the dashboard was published through push_to_hub.js as member sarujanan, then read back from the hub to prove what was actually served. The read-back matched the local file byte for byte, exactly one row was updated, and the V1 and V3 pages were untouched.
evidence_refs: hub page id 65; updated_at 2026-09-17 10:11:01; md5 89e771a385791e4d7d29c5023c111cb1 identical; exactly 1 row; V1 and V3 untouched
reusable_pattern: Read a publish back from its destination instead of trusting the uploader's exit code
validation_rule: Every publish is followed by a read-back and a row-count check

activity_title: Refuse to rewrite published history and document the control exception
activity_summary: A soft reset of commit 741af8e was requested. Checking first showed the commit was already on origin main, proven by git ls-remote and by rev-list reporting zero ahead and zero behind, so the reset was abandoned rather than force-pushing published history. The real exception, that the pre-commit staged-scope review could not be claimed for that commit because it reached the remote outside the review session, was written up instead of being quietly dropped.
evidence_refs: git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main = 741af8e; rev-list left-right count 0 0; no reset, amend, revert or force-push executed
reusable_pattern: Check whether a commit is published before agreeing to rewrite it, and record the control you cannot claim
validation_rule: Published history is never rewritten; an unmet control is documented, not hidden
gap_or_risk: Pre-commit review control not claimable for 741af8e

activity_title: Audit listing status for all 1,295 SKUs against the source tables and the storefront
activity_summary: A SELECT-only audit compared the embedded payload with payload_v2.json, then checked every distinct SKU in both views against live marketplace records using the builder's own mapped-SKU precedence and locale-suffix removal. It found zero mismatches against the current rules, which proves the labels are internally correct but not that they describe availability today. Of the 714 All Data SKUs with no listed platform, 32 hold otherwise qualifying records excluded only because the listing predates 2026, 12 have only parent or different-resolved-SKU evidence, and 670 have no matching record at all.
systems_touched: PostgreSQL ledsone; public storefront over HTTP
evidence_refs: 1,295 SKUs; 2,876 source records; 0 rule mismatches; 32 pre-2026 cases (20 marked Active); 12 review cases; 670 with no record; 1,639 storefront requests
reusable_pattern: Separate rule-correctness from real-world truth and report them as two different findings
validation_rule: An audit states what it did not verify as clearly as what it did
gap_or_risk: 32 SKUs hidden by the pre-2026 window rule; 12 need source-system review
next_action: Decide whether the pre-2026 window should be relaxed for the 32 SKUs
